chapter.title: 42  Data Driven Decision Making
figures: Figure 42.1: This author’s decision architecture separates estimates of consequences from their valuation within a human-defined mandate. Comparing actions also requires causal evidence. Human authorization and later review connect the analysis to accountable action; the diagram is a proposed workflow, not an experimentally established universal sequence.
Table 42.1: The same forecast can imply different actions under different values

Figure 42.2: An illustrative 30% rain forecast exceeds one organizer’s 20% action threshold but falls below another’s 60% threshold. The thresholds follow from the hypothetical error losses in the text, with zero incremental loss for correct matches. They are not observed behavior or recommendations for actual events.
Table 42.2: Questions to distinguish when applying the Flint lesson; the table is an analytical synthesis, not a description of a single adopted city policy

Figure 42.3: Hypothetical group-average dropout rates illustrate why baseline risk and intervention benefit can rank groups differently. The with-outreach rates require causal evidence; they cannot be inferred from the baseline forecasts alone. These values are constructed for teaching and are not findings about a student-support program.
Table 42.3: Select functions for a decision workflow; these tool families overlap
Table 42.4: An AI decision canvas that keeps prediction, valuation, causal evidence, and responsibility distinct
